# Leyla Fıratlı

> Leyla Fıratlı is a breathwork therapist and mind-body practitioner offering decolonial mind-body medicine for chronic pain, anxiety and panic. She works with clients online across all time zones and offers workshops as she moves around the world in Türkiye, the UK, the US and beyond.

Her work draws on Dr. John Sarno's work, conscious connected breathwork and somatic awareness. She trained through the SarnoXSachs Chronic Pain Practitioner Training and did two years of breathwork therapy training with Inspire Breathwork. This work is educational and not a substitute for medical care.

## Main pages

- [Work with me](https://leylafiratli.com/breathwork-therapy-for-chronic-pain.html): A 5-week online group breathwork therapy program for chronic pain, anxiety and panic attacks. Mind-body medicine with a decolonial lens. Online, wherever you are. Starts November 21, 2026, €75.
- [Free class: Mind Body Medicine 101](https://leylafiratli.com/free-practices.html): A free 50-minute class on chronic pain, anxiety and panic: how your nervous system can get stuck in protection, and how to tell if it's happening for you.
- [About Leyla](https://leylafiratli.com/about.html): How I found freedom from a year of debilitating back pain, and why I now offer decolonial mind-body medicine for chronic pain.
- [Resources](https://leylafiratli.com/resources.html): Books, journal prompts, and practices for mind-body healing from chronic pain, the tools that supported my own freedom and continue to help others.
- [Contact](https://leylafiratli.com/contact.html): Have a question about mind-body medicine for chronic pain, or want to see if we're a fit? Send a note, or book a free intro call online.
- [Writing](https://leylafiratli.com/writing.html): Writing on chronic pain, breath and the mind-body approach by Leyla Fıratlı, with longer essays on Substack.

## Writing

- [What is a mind-body approach to chronic pain?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/what-is-a-mind-body-approach-to-chronic-pain.html): A mind-body approach to chronic pain recognizes that not all pain comes from structural damage.
- [How do I know if my pain might be mind-body?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/how-do-i-know-if-my-pain-is-mind-body.html): Common signs of mind-body pain include pain that moves around the body, changes with stress or emotions, began during a hard period of life, or doesn't match what your scans show.
- [What does a decolonial approach to chronic pain mean?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/what-does-a-decolonial-approach-to-chronic-pain-mean.html): A decolonial approach to chronic pain sees pain as connected to your whole life and the world you live in, not only to a part of your body.
- [What is TMS, the name Dr. Sarno gave to mind-body pain?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/what-is-tms.html): TMS stands for tension myositis syndrome. It's the name Dr. John Sarno gave to chronic pain that is real and physical, but that comes from the nervous system responding to emotional tension rather than from structural damage.
- [Is this pain all in my head?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/is-chronic-pain-all-in-my-head.html): No. Mind-body pain is not imagined. It's a real, physical experience. What's different is where it comes from: a nervous system stuck on alert, rather than damage in the tissue.
- [Can back pain and sciatica be mind-body?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/can-back-pain-and-sciatica-be-mind-body.html): Yes. Back pain and sciatica are some of the most common ways mind-body pain shows up, including pain that runs from the lower back down the leg, like mine did.
- [Can mind-body work help if I have a diagnosis like a herniated disc or scoliosis?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/can-mind-body-work-help-if-i-have-a-diagnosis.html): Yes, it often can. Mind-body work doesn't deny what's on your scan, but many people with the very same findings live without pain.
- [Do I need to see a doctor before starting mind-body work?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/do-i-need-to-see-a-doctor-first.html): Yes, I recommend having a doctor rule out serious medical causes first. Knowing nothing dangerous is going on in your body makes it much easier to trust mind-body work and go deeper with it.
- [What does breath have to do with chronic pain?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/what-does-breath-have-to-do-with-pain.html): Conscious connected breathwork is a practice of feeling: a way into the emotions and nervous system patterns we usually keep out of awareness.
- [How I found freedom from a year of back and leg pain](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/how-i-found-freedom-from-a-year-of-back-and-leg-pain.html): In May 2024, I was struck with pain from my lower back down my right leg, and for almost a year I could barely walk.
- [Are panic attacks mind-body?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/are-panic-attacks-mind-body.html): Yes. A panic attack is your nervous system's alarm going off at full volume, and everything you feel during one is real and physical.
- [What is conscious connected breathwork?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/what-is-conscious-connected-breathwork.html): Conscious connected breathwork is a way of breathing with no pause between the inhale and the exhale, kept up for a sustained stretch of time, with the guidance of a certified practitioner.
- [Can migraines and tension headaches be mind-body?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/can-migraines-and-tension-headaches-be-mind-body.html): Often, yes. The nervous system plays a big part in both migraines and tension headaches, and many people notice that theirs follow stress or other triggers.
- [Can IBS and gut problems be mind-body?](https://leylafiratli.com/writing/can-ibs-and-gut-problems-be-mind-body.html): Gut symptoms are a very common way mind-body pain can show up. The gut and the brain are in constant conversation through the nervous system.
